case_title: MADALA VENKATA NARSIMHA RAO v. STATE OF A.P.
aggravating_circumstances: Accused ran away from the scene with blood-stained clothes, victim's dying declaration
high_court_outcome: Convicted under s.302 and s.376 IPC
neutral_facts: The accused was a laborer working for the victim's family. The victim was alone at home when her brother sent the accused to perform some work. Witnesses saw the accused running out of the house in blood-stained clothes after hearing the victim's cries. The accused pushed the witnesses away as they entered the house. The victim told the witnesses that the accused hit her with a chutney grinder after she slapped him. The victim later died en route to the hospital. A post-mortem report suggested rape, but the doctor who conducted the post-mortem did not testify. The trial court acquitted the accused, while the high court convicted him of murder and rape. The Supreme Court upheld the conviction for murder but found no evidence of rape.
